title: Peripheral artery disease: stage, side and ulcer
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's peripheral artery disease and any related ulcer.
note:
Chief Complaint: Right foot pain.

HPI: [Copied Forward] Patient is a 77-year-old female presenting with chronic discomfort in the right lower extremity. She reports consistent rest pain in the right foot, which persists even when she is not active. The patient notes that the symptoms are localized specifically to the right leg. She denies any skin breakdown or open wounds.

Vitals: BP 134/82, HR 76, SpO2 98% on room air, Temp 98.6 F.

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Negative
Cardiovascular: Negative
Respiratory: Negative
Musculoskeletal: Positive (right foot pain)
Neurological: Negative
Integumentary: Negative

Medication List:
- Aspirin 81mg daily
- Atorvastatin 40mg daily

Exam:
General: Alert and oriented x3, in no acute distress.
Right Lower Extremity: Palpable pedal pulses are diminished. Skin is intact without any break in surface. Notable atherosclerosis of the native leg arteries. No signs of skin breakdown or drainage.

Assessment:
1. Atherosclerosis of the right leg arteries with rest pain in the right foot.

Plan:
1. Continue current antiplatelet and lipid-lowering medications.
2. Refer to vascular surgery for further imaging of the right lower extremity.
3. Follow up in 4 weeks.

Electronically signed, 
R. Mensah, PA-C
May 14, 2026
explanations: Atherosclerosis of native arteries of the right leg with rest pain (HCC 264): I70.221.

distractors.why: Rest pain is documented: it is a higher stage (HCC 264).
